body.statement: For every distribution of \(O\) that is the observed-data pushforward of at least one law in \(\mathfrak M_H\), every such sustained-arm full-data extension, and every \(\gamma\in\mathcal G_H(p_{BT},q)\), the explicit algorithm \(\mathfrak L\) produces a finite-horizon FFRCISTG law on raw nonnegative-integer count paths with triple margin \(\gamma\), the same pushforward distribution of \(O\), absorbing death, baseline randomization, and the same arm-specific sequential censoring continuation probabilities conditional on the factual at-risk histories \(\mathcal H_{\ell-1}^a\). On each constructed switched survivor branch the raw post-\(k\) increment is exactly \(W\); no global restriction bounds raw counts by \(H\). Conversely, every law in \(\mathfrak M_H\) induces a member of \(\mathcal G_H(p_{BT},q)\). The construction imposes neither censoring independence from the entire response tree nor any other cross-world independence beyond baseline randomization and the listed FFRCISTG conditions.
body.justification: Polyhedral sharpness is causal only if every extremal summary coupling can be realized by a global finite-horizon response tree without silently invoking an NPSEM cross-world product structure.
body.gap: GreseleEtAl2022 studies causal-marginal gluing and RichardsonRobins2013 distinguishes FFRCISTG from NPSEM models; neither supplies an observed-law-preserving recurrent-event lift with death and censoring.
body.consumer: Every endpoint and regret optimizer over the transport polytope is certified as attainable by a causal model rather than only by an abstract coupling.
